messages.content: start Docker on window using docker start.

function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning:
The user says "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon itself. To start Docker service, you need to start the Docker Desktop or Docker Engine service. On Windows, you can use `net start com.docker.service` or `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`. Or if using Docker Desktop, you might open the application.

But the user likely wants to start Docker engine via command line. We can use PowerShell: `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`. Or using `sc start com.docker.service`.

We have a tool to execute commands on Windows OS. So we can call the function with command: `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`. But the tool expects a string of Windows command line instructions. It uses os.system() which runs shell commands. In PowerShell, we can use `powershell -Command "Start-Service -Name com.docker.service"`. Or just `powershell Start-Service -Name com.docker.service`. But os.system will run the command directly. If we pass `powershell -Command "Start-Service -Name com.docker.service"` it should work.

Alternatively, we can use `sc start com.docker.service`. That is simpler: `sc start com.docker.service`.

Thus we can call the function with command: `sc start com.docker.service`. Let's do that.
